Q7: The X(country) coup attempt is one of the most cinematic and chaotic 48-hour periods in modern political history.
On April 11, the military claimed Y had resigned and installed a business leader, and as expected, received quick recognition from US. However, that business leader overreached by dissolving the assembly, the supreme court and the constitution, alienating even coup supporters.
While private media backed the coup, Y's loyalists used community networks to spread the idea that Y hadn’t resigned. A smuggled note stating "I have not resigned the power that the people gave me," from Y sparked mass protests. Loyal Presidential Guards retook the palace, and Y was rescued from detention at a naval base on an island through a daring helicopter mission.
By April 14, Y was back in power, more powerful than ever(ruling until his death), and shifted the Bolivarian Revolution toward a more explicit socialist path.
